Indikator 9 tracks mortality rates (mortalitetsandel) across various geographical and administrative healthcare units in [[danmark|Danmark]], comparing the current reporting year against the two preceding periods (2022/23 and 2021/22) [^src1]. The data reveals a broad, consistent downward trend in mortality across the country, with the national average falling from 8.0% in 2021/22 to 7.6% in 2022/23, and reaching 7.3% in the current year [^src1]. No explicit target thresholds or met/missed flags are provided in this dataset; the evaluation is strictly comparative across time and geography [^src1].

At the regional level, all five regions mirror this national improvement. [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] reduced its mortality rate from 8.0% to 7.2% over the three periods, while [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] improved from 8.3% to 7.9% [^src1]. [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] both achieved current-year rates of 7.6% and 7.3%, respectively, continuing their steady declines from 8.4% and 7.7% in 2021/22 [^src1]. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] also saw a reduction, finishing the current year at 6.9%, down from 7.8% [^src1].

When examining the localized health clusters, the lowest mortality rates are found in [[sundhedsklyngen-holbaek|Sundhedsklyngen Holbæk]] at 6.2%, followed by [[sundhedsklynge-lillebaelt|Sundhedsklynge Lillebælt]] at 6.4%, and [[sundhedsklyngen-suh|Sundhedsklyngen SUH]] at 6.5% [^src1]. Conversely, the highest mortality rates are recorded in [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] and [[klynge-vest|Klynge VEST]], both tied at 8.7% [^src1]. [[sundhedsklynge-soenderjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland]] (8.2%) and [[sundhedsklynge-fyn|Sundhedsklynge Fyn]] (8.1%) also sit at the higher end of the spectrum [^src1].

While the overwhelming majority of clusters demonstrate continuous or eventual improvement, a few outliers break the downward pattern in the current year. [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] remained flat at 7.9% across the first two periods before spiking to 8.7% in the current year [^src1]. Similarly, [[klynge-vest|Klynge VEST]] dropped from 8.7% to 7.6% in 2022/23 but rebounded back to 8.7% in the current year [^src1]. Other clusters, such as [[klynge-midt|Klynge MIDT]], also saw slight current-year increases, moving from 7.5% in 2022/23 to 7.9% in the current year [^src1].

Comprehensive background, methodology, and additional indicators from the 2023 and 2024 Danish healthcare quality reports are documented across multiple sections [^src2] [^src3] [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11] [^src12] [^src13] [^src14] [^src15] [^src16] [^src17] [^src18] [^src19].
